attempts.raw_response: This uncertainty has sparked fierce debate among medical professionals and patient advocacy groups alike. Critics argue that removing the dedicated funding stream could leave life-saving treatments out of reach for those who need them most, particularly in cases where NICE has deemed a drug too expensive or lacking sufficient evidence. The committee’s report highlights the urgent need for a transparent framework that balances fiscal responsibility with ethical obligations to patients. Without clear guidelines, hospitals may struggle to allocate resources effectively, leading to inconsistent care across different regions. Stakeholders are calling for immediate dialogue between government officials, pharmaceutical companies, and healthcare providers to ensure that no one is left behind during this transition period.

pair.human_continuation: Committee chairman Stephen Dorrell said: "Where an individual patient is on a course of treatment it is important there isn't a cliff edge, that the patient has continuity of care." The Department of Health said it would "ensure arrangements are in place to protect individual patients who are receiving treatment with drugs funded by the Cancer Drugs Fund as the end of the fund approaches." The new drug pricing system due to come in is known as value-based pricing. This aims to give NHS patients better access to effective and innovative medicines. It means the clinical worth of a drug will be taken into account when setting a price tag. But the health select committee says the government has done little to explain how the system will work in practice, despite the plans being under discussion since 2010.
pair.prefix: The new pricing system is set to start in 2014 and could affect many medicines used by the NHS, not just cancer drugs. But a big concern is that it replaces the temporary Cancer Drug Fund, which was introduced in 2011 to help people access cancer drugs currently not approved by the health regulator the National Institute for Health and Clinical Excellence (NICE). The Health Select Committee says the lack of clarity on the future of the scheme puts cancer patients and doctors in the dark.

source_document.title: Cancer drug fund future 'uncertain' as new scheme 'ill-defined'
